sourceFacts.fact: Misaligned eyes can provide conflicting images, and the developing visual system can suppress one eye's input.
Suppression is functional reduced use of information, not severing of an optic nerve.

expectedLabels: Strabismic amblyopia: unequal use of input

LEFT upper postcard contains a crisp upright toy-star icon labelled 'Aligned input'. LEFT lower postcard contains the same star with a faint offset duplicate labelled 'Conflicting input'. UPPER lane is a broad solid teal ribbon carrying a crisp star toward a plain rectangular learning tile at RIGHT labelled 'Visual learning'. LOWER lane is an ochre ribbon that becomes pale and thin as it approaches the SAME tile, with its star fading, label 'Suppression'. Both lanes reach the tile boundary; neither is cut or physically broken. Bottom 'Information model • not nerve anatomy'.
